faq.q: What is the origin of Moushumi?
faq.a: Moushumi is associated with Bengali. Moushumi is Bengali মৌসুমী (moushumi), meaning 'seasonal'.
No — the underlying form is Bengali, not Arabic.
Moushumi can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Bengali-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Moushumi should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Moushumi is a Bengali word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Moushumi mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Moushumi is rendered ماشومی and carries the sense ماشومی، فصلی.
A romanized syllable approximation is mous-hu-mi. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Moushumi, moushumi. Script forms are ماشومي, ماشومی, مَاشُومِي, मौशुमी.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
